# 4 Tips to Ace Your Registered Dietitian Exam


[Careers](https://www.hcsgcorp.com/blog/category/careers/) ,


[Nutrition](https://www.hcsgcorp.com/blog/category/nutrition/)


You’ve made it through the coursework and supervised practice. Now there’s one more step between you and your RD credential: the exam.


It can feel like a lot to prepare for, especially when a question asks you to choose the *best* answer from several that sound reasonable. That’s why we asked Registered Dietitians at Healthcare Services Group (HCSG) what helped them study, stay on track, and approach test day with confidence.


**1. Set a weekly study goal you can actually keep**


A study plan is useful only if it fits your life. Start by looking at the time you have between now and your exam, then set a weekly goal you can work around your other commitments. Leave room to spend extra time on topics that take longer than expected.


HCSG RD Ava Govek learned that lesson during her own preparation: ***“I greatly underestimated how much time it would take to cover each domain, which made me fall off my study schedule. I found that it worked best for me to set an hourly study goal each week and then found time to fit it into my schedule.”***


If you miss a study session, adjust your plan and pick it back up. Consistent progress matters more than a perfect calendar.


**2. Practice answering questions, not just reviewing notes**


Knowing the material is important but understanding it matters most. As you study, work through practice questions and take time to understand why an answer is the best choice. Pay attention to the topics and question types that repeatedly stump you, then use those patterns to guide your next study session.


A study partner can help, too. Ava recommends that candidates ***“connect with a study partner to bounce ideas off of and to keep you motivated.”*** Explaining your reasoning out loud can show you what you understand and what you need to review.


**3. Choose resources you’ll use consistently**


There’s no prize for using a ton of study materials. HCSG RD Lauren Isabella found it more helpful to focus on one tool, while Ava used several. Try a resource, see whether it helps you learn and practice, and build a routine around what works for you.


Resources candidates may want to explore include:


- **All Access Dietetics:** RD exam study tools
- **Chomp Down Dietetics Podcast:** Practice questions you can listen to on the go
- **Jean Inman:** Recorded study guide sessions
- **Pocket Prep:** Question-based practice
- **Visual Veggies:** Study materials in a range of formats


**4. Know when to stop studying and start trusting yourself**


It’s easy to keep reviewing because you feel there must be one more thing you should know. Lauren says one of her biggest challenges was deciding when she had prepared enough:


***“The biggest challenge I encountered was knowing when I had studied enough and avoiding information overload. You don’t need to know every single piece of information to pass the exam. Read each question carefully, eliminate the answers you know are incorrect, and choose the best answer based on your knowledge and gut.”***


This useful approach forces you to slow down, read what the question is asking, rule out what you can, and make your best choice.


HCSG RD Jessica Nicholson offers one final reminder: ***“If you study consistently and have confidence in yourself, you will do better than you think!”***


The RD exam is a big milestone, but you’ve already done a great deal of work to reach it. Give yourself a plan you can follow, practice making decisions, and let your preparation carry you into test day.
